chunks: And that which was narrated is: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Kulayb al-Asadi who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the ritual slaughter (of the Qurbani), so he said: 'As for Mina, then [it is for] three days, and as for the provinces (outside Mina), then [it is for] one day.'

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.النَّحْر: Ritual slaughter of the animal for sacrifice (Qurbani)
key_terms.الْبُلْدَانِ: The provinces or regions outside Mina
key_terms.بِمِنًى: In Mina (the specific location for Hajj rituals)

ai.seo_question: What are the days for offering the Hajj sacrifice (Qurbani) in Mina versus outside Mina?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the temporal distinction for ritual slaughter (Nahr) between the sacred precincts of Mina and other regions. It establishes that while pilgrims in Mina have three days (10th–12th Dhu al-Hijjah) to sacrifice, those in the provinces (Buldan) are restricted to a single day, reflecting the practical flexibility granted to non-residents in Shia fiqh. This ruling underscores the importance of location in determining the duration of the Hajj sacrifice period.
